A brand new chapter in the world of apex legends, and they could not anticipate that the game would draw back many gamers, especially with references to to titanfall 2, is it not to be expected that the surge of players would rise exponentially and plan accordingly? a similar event happened in season five and its was no biggy, but for it to happen again in season nine in what may be the biggest season for apex? the devs must have their head in the ground. Do you think they want to fix any of the problems above? Good one.

They're introducing a new money-grabbing monetisation system instead. They're making battle passes even more FOMO.

You can no longer use their now useless in-game currency to buy them, you can no longer pay for the battle passes with free currency you earned from completing them. You get 2 battle passes per season each one only lasting ~6 weeks and costing $10, so $80/year if you want to get everything.

They're milking the whales before the game eventually dies instead of actually trying to make the game playable.

After 1000+ hours in Apex Legends, I think I’ve seen everything this game has to offer—the hype, the frustration, the third-parties, the cracked teams, the broken metas, and those rare god-tier matches that remind you why you keep coming back.

Apex is one of the smoothest, most satisfying movement shooters ever made. Sliding, climbing, beaming someone across the map—it all feels insanely good. The gunplay is tight, the legends feel unique, and when a squad wipe goes perfectly, it’s pure dopamine.

But I’ll be honest: Apex can also be a rollercoaster of pain. Matchmaking sometimes throws you into the shadow realm, the meta shifts can be questionable, and if you queue solo… well, may the Apex gods have mercy on you.

Even with its flaws, no other BR matches the speed, fluidity, and chaos of Apex. When the stars align—great teammates, great loot, great rotation—it becomes one of the best competitive shooters out there. And despite every rage moment, I clearly love it, because here I am, 1000+ hours deep and still dropping in.

Apex is messy, fast, frustrating, addictive, and absolutely unmatched. If you can handle the tilt, it might just become your second home like it did for me.

I have almost 360 hours in Apex, so giving it a negative review feels a little ridiculous. I clearly loved this game.

But Arenas was what kept me coming back.

3v3 Arenas gave Apex something completely different. You still had the movement, gunplay, legends and everything that makes Apex feel so good, but without having to commit to the battle royale every time you wanted to play.

Then they removed it.

Maybe Arenas wasn't the direction they wanted Apex to go, but for me it was the best part of the game. Once it was gone, so was the reason I kept playing. I eventually uninstalled Apex and haven't had any real desire to come back.

Bring back 3v3 Arenas and I'll probably have it downloaded again before the announcement is over.

Until then, Apex and I are not on speaking terms...
